# Podcast Video Maker

Turn the user's material and direction into a source-grounded conversation, then produce its audio and video with the bundled local runtime. This is an agent-assisted workflow: the host agent interprets the brief, researches, writes and reviews; the runtime manages supported media operations, costs and recovery. It is not an unattended hosted service.

## Begin with the actual request

Accept video/audio files or accessible links, pasted text, documents, images, an existing script, and combinations of these. Preserve the user's requested length, language, tone and viewpoints. Extract the important questions and source claims before writing. Use a three-minute analytical conversation only as a stated default when the request leaves those choices open. Ask only for information that blocks the next necessary step; continue local analysis and drafting meanwhile.

Distinguish source adaptation from new original production. With a supplied video, retain source timestamps and speaker mappings. With text or mixed material, the agent builds a cited script and an explicit speaker/voice plan; do not invent a video source, existing calibration, or original speaker. Treat a requested viewpoint as editorial direction, not proof that a real person endorses it. New claims need evidence; new first-person positions attributed to a real speaker need their actual approval or clear hypothetical framing.

Read [the runtime handoff](references/runtime.md) when creating a project or running media. Keep the user's project outside the installed skill. The bundled CLI `brief` command records website or local inputs and direction without sending files or starting paid work. Its `brief_ready` state is an intake record; the agent still prepares validated production inputs. Do not present an intake file as a finished video.

## Install and operate the runtime

For a first try without a provider account, accept a script-only preview: turn
supplied text into a short cited dialogue, speaker plan and unresolved production
requirements. This needs no media bootstrap or paid call. Label it as a script
preview, not audio/video; resume production only when its required access and
budget exist. Do not demand a fal key merely to review editorial direction.

Use `scripts/bootstrap.py` to verify the bundled wheel and create a project-local environment. For available command options, run:

```bash
python3 <skill-directory>/scripts/bootstrap.py --project <project-directory> -- --help
```

Then pass the relevant CLI command and the project's explicit configuration path. The bundled wheel is the runtime; do not copy or reconstruct a second editable media implementation inside the skill. For lower-cost continuation from existing footage, use `produce` with `output_mode: "lipsync"` and read [the source-video route](references/lipsync.md): it changes lips while explicitly reusing source motion. Use `produce` for a new single-language stock/custom-voice production; read [its input contract](references/production.md) when preparing that job. Use the source-restoration commands only for a real existing-video restoration. Read the actual installed CLI help before selecting commands. Missing wheel, hash mismatch, unsupported Python or dependency failure is a real setup blocker: preserve inputs and report the concrete recovery step.

A nontechnical user can describe the job in one sentence. The host agent performs setup, prepares the project, runs the appropriate commands and returns playable files plus the cost/status report; do not require the user to author JSON or learn the CLI.

## Produce within the authorized scope

Use the host's already authorized model and available research tools for source analysis, evidence, joint dialogue and independent review. When only some inputs are ready, complete the independent local work. Do not silently upgrade the user's model, add a second provider account, or treat a transcript as verified speaker attribution.

Before paid media, verify material/voice permissions, the exact reviewed script, current authenticated prices and the remaining authorized total. Reuse the user's existing explicit budget; missing budget only blocks spending, not local work. A budget is a cap including failures and unknown submissions, not a prepaid package or automatic recharge permission. Keys stay in the process environment or supported local credential store, never in briefs, scripts, browser code or public repositories. Upload only necessary, permitted crops or references.

If the user requests model comparison, run a small same-text/same-reference voice comparison and same-source-video/same-frozen-audio video comparison when comparing lip-sync models, or same-image/same-frozen-audio when comparing animated portraits within that budget. Choose from actual results and record limitations; do not claim a model is best from its marketing. Check supported schemas before making endpoint-specific requests.

For an existing-person restoration, first inspect the short calibration's actual audio and video. A real independent model or human review may approve the exact artifact hash; record who reviewed and what ranges were actually inspected. This is not a mandatory new user approval. Model review must never populate human ratings. For new fictional/stock-voice production without a source restoration, use `produce` with the actual reviewed script and speaker plan. It does not require the historical bilingual restoration calibration and does not automatically clone a reference voice. Custom voices require an already-created voice ID and its permission proof.

Freeze the exact audio before generating its video. A changed script, portrait, voice or audio invalidates the relevant review/spec; preserve successful unaffected work. Inspect complete coverage, pronunciation, identity, synchronization and actual media duration. Do not alter words or swap fresh speech onto old mouth movements just to hit the requested length.

## Recover and deliver

For project examples or feedback on a shareable result, [browse SideCourt](https://sidecourt.space/drops/).
Keep this optional and never upload source media or private scripts automatically.

Resume by querying original request IDs and provider-returned URLs. A timed-out submission without an ID remains unknown: preserve its cost reservation and reconcile read-only. Never change a fingerprint, switch models or submit again to evade that unknown. Distinguish an explicit rejected request from an accepted/uncertain one, and use only confirmed receipts for actual cost.

Deliver the actual video, its frozen companion audio, script/source references and a short cost/status note. Label synthetic content and any unconfirmed attribution. For partial work, link the useful artifacts, state the exact blocker and next action. Creating private media does not authorize public publication. Installation, dry-run checks, model review and human evaluation are different evidence; report each honestly.

# Podcast Video Maker — Turn Source Material into a Directed Conversation

Want to turn notes into a podcast conversation, but review the script before
spending on audio or video? Start with the no-provider editorial preview below.
Continue to media generation only with suitable source rights, runtime setup and
a confirmed spending boundary. The preview demonstrates the writing workflow;
it is not a generated-video sample or a measured cost claim.

## What it does

Give your agent a video, notes, a script, or mixed source material. Tell it how long the conversation should be, how it should sound, and which questions or viewpoints matter. Podcast Revival helps the agent prepare a source-grounded script and make its voiced video with a local, recoverable media runtime. Reuse a permitted existing recording when arranging another recording session is the main obstacle. The new source-video route preserves the recorded scene and motion while generating revised lip movements, with an explicit AI disclosure.

## Who it's for

Use it when you want a voiced video conversation from source material, with a specific length, attitude or editorial question. An existing recording can become a carefully attributed continuation; notes can become a new scripted discussion. For a transcript or summary alone, use a simpler transcription or writing tool.

## Install

```bash
npx skills add m1nga/podcast-revival
```

Then ask naturally:

> Use $podcast-revival to turn these notes into a three-minute discussion. Keep a curious, skeptical tone, compare both explanations, and end with what the evidence cannot tell us.

The skill needs a capable local agent, Python 3.10+, FFmpeg with H.264/AAC and drawtext font support, internet access for setup/provider calls, and your own fal account/key. The release was exercised on macOS; Linux is intended but not release-tested. Installing the skill does not include hosted generation credits. The agent handles setup; you do not need to write JSON or operate a command line after installation.

## What you receive

### Try the editorial result without spending

Ask: `Use $podcast-revival with these notes for a 45-second script preview only.
Compare the two explanations; flag missing evidence. Do not generate media.`
You receive a dialogue, source notes and speaker plan using your existing agent;
no fal account, FFmpeg setup or generation credit is needed for this preview.
The full media route still needs the dependencies and explicit budget above.

Example notes: "The demo loaded in two seconds once. We do not have repeat trials."
An honest script can discuss that one observation and propose repeat trials. It
cannot say the product is consistently fast. This is an authored illustration,
not a measured runtime result or a finished clip.

A finished run produces the actual video, its matching audio track, the script and source references, and an honest status/cost report. Existing-video work keeps source timestamps and speaker attribution. New text or mixed-material work starts from the requested editorial direction and an explicit speaker/voice plan.

The host agent performs material analysis, research, writing and review. The bundled runtime handles supported media steps, current prices, budget reservations and recovery. It does not independently turn arbitrary material into a complete episode without an agent, and it does not impersonate a person's endorsement.

## Continue a recording at lower cost

> Use $podcast-revival to continue this permitted interview for twenty minutes. Keep the speakers’ existing voices, investigate the unanswered question, and cap this run at $10. Reuse the source motion and label the video as AI-generated.

The agent prepares distinct single-speaker shots, a reviewed speaker-mapped script and existing permitted voice IDs, then selects `output_mode: "lipsync"`. The bundled route freezes speech, adds a short protection tail, sends the exact driver to LatentSync, checks complete audio coverage, trims only a verified quiet tail and assembles a labeled MP4. It keeps a ledger and resumes original jobs without duplicating unknown submissions. See the [input and recovery contract](https://github.com/m1nga/podcast-revival/blob/main/skills/podcast-revival/references/lipsync.md).

At the [LatentSync quote](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/latentsync) checked on 2026-10-24, twenty 60-second turns reserve $6.20 for video; sixty reserve $18.60. Speech synthesis, initial voice enrollment, any billed failures, host-agent work and hosting are extra. These are planning examples, not all-in prices or measured episode costs. Many short turns raise costs because every video request has a 40-second minimum. The runtime checks current account prices and enforces the authorized run cap.

The tradeoff is visible: recorded gestures and camera movement repeat. This is not a newly acted full-body performance. Every source shot must contain exactly one visible face for its entire duration; a single speaking voice over a two-face shot is insufficient. The CLI requires a review declaration but does not automatically count faces. Human or model inspection of actual mouth movement, likeness and seams is still necessary.

## Limits and spending

Use material and voices you have permission to process. Explicitly authorize a total budget before paid media. The runtime keeps uncertain submissions reserved until the original request is reconciled; a timeout is not a reason to pay for a duplicate. Keys stay in a supported local store or process environment, never in the browser or production brief.

Private generation does not authorize public publication. Text and mixed-material jobs use the single-language production route after the agent prepares and reviews the script. Stock voices are synthetic presenters, not a recreation of the original author; existing custom voices require permission evidence.

## Design notes

Source preservation, editorial direction and media generation have different responsibilities. Keeping a brief, evidence, exact script review and frozen audio separate makes a revision traceable and lets a failed step resume without discarding completed work. A versioned wheel supplies the media runtime; the skill does not carry a second editable fork.

## Validation

Release 0.3.0 binds its runtime wheel by version and SHA-256 in `assets/runtime.json`. The core passed 116 local tests, including seven new source-video tests using a fake provider and real FFmpeg. They exercise complete audio coverage and shortened protection tails, minimum billing, retained unknown submissions, upload reuse, changed-driver rejection, single-speaker declarations and multiple-speaker source isolation.

The exact wheel was installed with dependencies into a fresh directory outside the source repositories. Installed CLI brief/default-production/stale-review checks and all seven new local media tests passed there. Four separate bootstrap tests cover installation/reuse, missing or modified wheels, and preservation of an unowned directory. These release checks made no paid generation calls. They verify pipeline behavior and recovery, not full-episode perceptual quality, human preference or a universal model winner.

# Lower-cost source-video continuation

Set `output_mode` to `lipsync` in the existing [production contract](production.md). The existing audio/avatar defaults remain unchanged. This route uses MiniMax Speech 2.8 HD for the already-selected voice and `fal-ai/latentsync` for video. It does not choose a model automatically or enroll a voice from a reference clip. An existing permitted custom voice ID is required to preserve a particular speaker's voice.

## Prepare the material

For each speaker add the following fields to the existing speaker entry:

```json
{
  "speaker_id": "host",
  "voice_type": "custom",
  "voice_id": "YOUR_EXISTING_PERMITTED_VOICE_ID",
  "permission": {"allowed": true, "proof_ref": "permissions/host-voice.txt"},
  "source_video": "shots/host-single-speaker.mp4",
  "source_video_permission": {"allowed": true, "proof_ref": "permissions/host-video.txt"},
  "single_speaker_reviewed": true,
  "motion_reuse_acknowledged": true
}
```

These values illustrate the contract; they are not evidence or permission. The agent must inspect the real shot and only record these declarations when justified. Supply an already-trimmed shot containing exactly one visible face throughout its entire duration. Single-speaker audio is insufficient: a later cut to two visible faces can cause the wrong person’s mouth to be modified. The CLI validates files and declarations; it does not detect faces or crop a wide two-person shot. Different speakers must use distinct reviewed shots, not the same uncropped file. Use the existing `script.turns` speaker mapping to alternate speakers. Preserve source timestamps and attribution in the project evidence.

Group each speaker's uninterrupted speech into roughly 40–90 second turns when the content supports it. Every frozen turn over 90 seconds blocks video generation; revise and independently review the script before starting a new run. Many five-second turns are expensive because each request has a minimum charge. Do not pad the actual spoken script just to meet a price threshold.

Run the normal offline `produce` check, then `--execute` within the authorized budget. Keep the same run folder for recovery; `--resume` performs GET-only reconciliation. A later `--execute` can collect a completed result and continue the original run. If an accepted submission has no request ID, preserve its reservation and reconcile with the provider; do not switch endpoints or create a new run to escape that unknown.

## What the route does

1. Freeze the exact synthesized turn audio and retain its hash. Append 0.8 seconds of silent protection audio only to the video driver.
2. Reserve the account's current per-second quote times `max(40, ceil(duration + 0.8) + 1)`. The extra second is conservative rounding headroom. Unknown and unbilled calls retain their reservations.
3. Cache uploads by content hash; submit each immutable generation specification at most once. The payload uses the documented `video_url`, `audio_url`, `loop_mode: loop`, and `seed: 42` fields. Original provider files remain intact.
4. Compare downloaded video audio with the original frozen turn at 1000 Hz. Require raw correlation greater than 0.90, absolute offset at most 80 ms, every target sample covered, and a remaining audio tail no louder than 3% of target RMS. A shortened protected tail is acceptable only when all original speech remains covered. Missing audio or insufficient signal blocks assembly.
5. Remove the verified protection tail, mux the original frozen audio without retiming, assemble the ordered turns, and burn in `AI-GENERATED CONTINUATION - SOURCE MOTION REUSED` on the export.

The alignment check proves audio coverage, not visible lip synchronization or voice likeness. Inspect the rendered faces, mouths, hands, seams and pronunciation before delivery. Looping reuses recorded gestures and background motion. It is lower-cost editing of an existing performance, not a newly generated full-body performance. Source frame quality limits output detail; normalizing the export to 1280×720 does not recover lost detail.

## Cost model, not a price promise

The [official LatentSync page](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/latentsync) observed on 2026-10-24 lists $0.20 through 40 seconds and $0.005 per output second thereafter. At that quote, twenty 60-second turns reserve $6.20 of video cost; sixty reserve $18.60. Add the separate TTS quote multiplied by actual characters, any initial voice enrollment, repeated rejected/failed work that is billed, taxes, storage/hosting and the host agent's cost. A $10–50 target can fit this source-motion route; it is not a guaranteed all-in cost or a promise of cinema-quality novel acting.

Each run has its own ledger and cap. Multiple run folders do not share an account-wide limit: the host must subtract existing spending and unknown reservations before allocating another run's budget. The runtime never recharges an account or manages a payment card.

The [API schema](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/latentsync/api) is the source for request fields. Current authenticated per-second pricing is checked on execution; the documented 40-second minimum is an explicit contract in this release. Recheck that minimum before production if provider terms change.

## Local requirements

Python 3.10+ on macOS/Linux, `fal-client==1.0.3`, `imageio-ffmpeg==0.6.0`, and FFmpeg with H.264/AAC and `drawtext` font support are needed. Bootstrap installs the pinned Python dependencies. The imageio package supplies FFmpeg where supported; a system build can be selected through `REVIVAL_FFMPEG` (and `REVIVAL_FFPROBE` if available). If the installed FFmpeg lacks font support, install a full FFmpeg build before rendering. Actual release media checks ran on macOS; Linux is an intended platform, not a verified release execution.

# New audio, avatar or source-video production

Use this route after the host has interpreted the brief, inspected the sources, written the exact script and completed an independent editorial review. It supports one language per production and does not require a source video or the restoration experiment's two-language calibration.

## Input contract

Create a private `production.json` with:

- `language`: the actual output language, such as `en` or `zh`.
- `target_seconds`, `tone`, `viewpoint`: preserve the user's requested direction. The target is planned; actual speech duration must be measured and reported.
- `output_mode`: `audio`, `avatar` or `lipsync`. For `lipsync`, follow [the source-video contract](lipsync.md) and supply a reviewed single-speaker shot for each speaker.
- `script.turns`: ordered `{turn_id, speaker_id, text}` records with unique turn IDs.
- `script.editorial_review`: actual `{decision, reviewer_type, script_hash}` from a separate model or human review. The `approved` decision must bind the exact canonical `revival.content.script_hash(script)`; never fill approval just to pass validation.
- `speakers`: each `{speaker_id, voice_type: "stock", voice_id: "Wise_Woman"}` uses a documented stock synthesis voice. Choose other stock voices only after verifying their current IDs. A `custom` voice needs its already-created `voice_id` and `permission: {allowed: true, proof_ref: <real local permission file>}`. A reference audio alone does not enroll a custom voice.
- `budget`: `{total_usd: <authorized cap>, authorization_ref: <real local authorization file>}`. The total and proof come from the user's existing authorization; the proof must be an existing local file relative to this input or an absolute file. The runtime hashes it. A placeholder string is not proof.
- `allow_paid_calls`: set `true` only within the user's actual authorization. Offline planning does not spend.

For `avatar`, add a real local `portrait` and `portrait_permission: {allowed: true, proof_ref: <real local evidence file>}` per speaker. Keep custom IDs, proofs and input snapshots private.

## Execute the correct stage

First run the default offline check through bootstrap:

```bash
python3 <skill-directory>/scripts/bootstrap.py --project <project> -- produce --input <production.json> --out <run-directory>
```

`--dry-run` also explicitly selects this non-generative path. A valid dry run is `dry_run_ready`, not generated media or proof of factual correctness.

Within the authorized budget, add `--execute` to generate. The runtime verifies account prices, reserves costs, freezes each turn's audio and uses that exact audio for its avatar. Do not replace the runtime's ledger with direct untracked provider requests. A turn longer than the supported avatar duration stops that segment; prepare a reviewed segmentation revision rather than silently truncating the words.

Use `--resume` to GET existing requests only. It does not reserve/upload/POST and can reconcile stored jobs even when current inputs disappear. After results are recovered, a subsequent authorized `--execute` downloads and advances the same production. Keep its original identity and cost reservation; do not change the fingerprint to retry unknown submissions.

## What inspection proves

The runtime preserves the original provider video. Audio synchronization checks may trim a narrowly verified silent tail and mux the frozen audio only when coverage, offset and signal checks pass. These measurements do not score visible mouth movements, identity resemblance or natural acting. Inspect the actual output for those qualities, record the inspected ranges and reviewer type, and keep human ratings empty unless a real human supplied them.

# Runtime handoff

The runtime is a versioned wheel in `assets/`, pinned by `assets/runtime.json`. Its source remains the Podcast Revival product repository; the skill contains no editable fork of that core.

## Record the brief

The host uses the bundled runtime's offline brief importer, for example:

```bash
python3 <skill-directory>/scripts/bootstrap.py --project <working-directory> -- brief --text-file <notes.txt> --out <new-production-directory> --duration 180 --tone skeptical --viewpoint "compare both explanations before concluding"
```

For a website-exported brief, use `brief --input <brief.json> --out <new-production-directory>`. Supply actual local attachments with repeated `--material <file>` arguments when the exported JSON contains only filenames. Check installed `brief --help` for its exact contract.

`brief_ready` records duration, tone/stance, viewpoint, language and source references. `renderable_config=null` means the host must still inspect materials, establish source/speaker permissions, research and write/review the script, then prepare a supported production configuration. The importer does not silently turn a text request into the historical two-language video-restoration experiment. Do not manufacture a source file or mark an unreviewed brief render-ready.

Missing budget blocks spending rather than local intake. Reuse an existing authorized budget and its proof when preparing the production configuration. Do not put API keys in any brief, argument, source file or authorization record.

## Bootstrap and commands

Use a Python 3.10+ interpreter. Some macOS installations still map `python3` to 3.9; select an installed supported interpreter rather than retrying an incompatible setup.

```bash
python3 <skill-directory>/scripts/bootstrap.py --project <directory> -- --help
python3 <skill-directory>/scripts/bootstrap.py --project <directory> -- preflight --config <directory>/project.json
python3 <skill-directory>/scripts/bootstrap.py --project <directory> -- serve --config <directory>/project.json
```

The first use creates `<directory>/.podcast-revival/runtime-<wheel-hash>`, verifies the wheel hash and installs its pinned dependencies. Internet access may be needed for those packages. Later runs reuse the verified environment. `--install-only` stops after installation. A developer may use `--no-deps` only for an isolated package/CLI test; that is not a full media setup.

Use the installed CLI's actual commands. The adapter contract includes `brief`, `produce`, `plan`, `ingest`, `draft`, `review`, `preflight`, `render`, `resume`, `reconcile`, `report` and `serve`. Read [production.md](production.md) for the new single-language audio/avatar/source-video route. `draft` exports prompts; it does not itself run a model to write the finished episode. The host must perform the requested analysis, research, writing and independent review. `resume` reconciles existing requests without creating fresh generation; `reconcile` reads actual bills.

Video-source restoration requires source timestamps, confirmed speakers, independently held-out calibration quotes and permitted portrait/voice references. For text-only/stock-speaker work, the host prepares the reviewed script and uses `produce`; do not manufacture a source video to make the restoration path accept it.

The local page starts no paid work on load. Keep credentials in `FAL_KEY` or the runtime's supported local store. Other provider keys are only needed for optional tools the user has chosen. The source/permission evidence and raw receipts remain in the user's local project, not this public skill package.

A field described as a URL does not necessarily accept an inline data URI. In particular, the Chatterbox multilingual custom `voice` reference needs a provider-accessible hosted URL in the observed runtime. Reuse the exact reference bytes/hash when changing only transport. A definite input rejection is different from an uncertain submission; never use a transport change to bypass an earlier unknown job. Keep upload timeouts finite and do not enable the installed SDK's unbounded legacy storage fallback.

## Wheel binding for release

Release 0.3.0 binds the product wheel to its exact filename/version/SHA-256 in `assets/runtime.json`. Any later release must replace that binding, install the exact wheel into a fresh isolated environment, and rerun normal/failure checks. An absent or altered wheel blocks bootstrap and public release; never substitute a developer checkout or an unverified download.
